name: Vermicelli Soup
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: lamb, from which every particle of fat has been removed
ingredients.originalText: 4 lbs. lamb, from which every particle of fat has been removed

ingredients.name: about a third of a pound of vermicelli or macaroni
ingredients.originalText: about a third of a pound of vermicelli or macaroni

instructions.text: Cut up the meat, cover it with a quart of water, and set it back on the range to heat very gradually, keeping it covered closely
At the end of an hour, add four quarts of boiling water, and cook until the meat is in shreds
Season with salt, sweet herbs, a chopped shallot, and two teaspoonfuls Worcestershire sauce
When these have boiled in the soup for ten minutes, strain and return to the fire
Have ready about a third of a pound of vermicelli which has been boiled tender in clear water
Add this; boil up once, and pour out

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut up the meat, cover it with a quart of water, and set it back on the range to heat very gradually, keeping it covered closely
2. At the end of an hour, add four quarts of boiling water, and cook until the meat is in shreds
3. Season with salt, sweet herbs, a chopped shallot, and two teaspoonfuls Worcestershire sauce
4. When these have boiled in the soup for ten minutes, strain and return to the fire
5. Have ready about a third of a pound of vermicelli which has been boiled tender in clear water
6. Add this; boil up once, and pour out
